2609.24859.title: Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks to Support Ideation
2609.24859.paper_summary: The ideation phase of participatory AI risk assessment often starts with a blank slate or a limited list of predefined risks, making it difficult to surface indirect or systemic harms. To address this limitation, we propose a three-stage ideation support tool. The tool complements participatory AI, rather than replacing it, and helps focus later engagement with affected communities. First, it dynamically discovers stakeholders depending on the given AI use and recursively expanding outward, allowing overlooked or indirect stakeholders to emerge. Second, it simulates these stakeholders with LLMs, connecting them into a network of a given topology, and having them ideate about risks. Third, it prioritizes risks using network centrality measures. In an initial evaluation, we found that betweenness centrality run through agents connected in a small-world network works best as it elevates risks raised by stakeholders who bridge disconnected groups, surfacing novel, systemic harms that traditional methods often miss. On an AI chatbot companion use case, this approach increased the novelty of the identified risks by approximately 1.1 points over single LLM brainstorming, and by 0.5 points over agentic LLM brainstorming, measured on a normalized five-point Likert scale, without reducing the plausibility or severity of the identified risks. To test whether our framework helps a human-led ideation session using the Futures Wheel approach, we divided 11 teams of non-western young chatbot users into two types: control (team) and treatment (team) in a participatory AI risk assessment. The control teams started from a list of risks generated by the 45 AI practitioners in the initial evaluation; the treatment teams started from a list generated by our framework. The treatment teams identified more risks overall, and more systemic, human-computer interaction, and environmental risks.
2609.24859.paper_summary_zh: 參與式 AI 風險評估的構思階段通常從一個空白的起點或有限的預定風險列表開始，這使得揭示間接或系統性危害變得困難。為了解決這一限制，我們提出了一個三階段的構思支持工具。該工具補充了參與式 AI，而不是取代它，並幫助專注於與受影響社區的後續參與。首先，它根據給定的 AI 使用情境動態發現利益相關者，並向外遞歸擴展，讓被忽視或間接的利益相關者浮現出來。其次，它使用大型語言模型（LLMs）模擬這些利益相關者，將它們連接成一個特定拓撲的網絡，並讓它們對風險進行構思。第三，它使用網絡中心性度量來優先考慮風險。在初步評估中，我們發現通過連接在小世界網絡中的代理運行的中介中心性效果最佳，因為它提升了由橋接不連通群體的利益相關者提出的風險，揭示了傳統方法常常忽視的新型系統性危害。在一個 AI 聊天機器人伴侶的使用案例中，這種方法使識別的風險的新穎性提高了約 1.1 分，相較於單一 LLM 腦力激盪，並且相較於代理 LLM 腦力激盪提高了 0.5 分，這是基於標準化的五點李克特量表測量的，且不降低識別風險的合理性或嚴重性。為了測試我們的框架是否有助於使用未來輪（Futures Wheel）方法的人主導構思會議，我們將 11 支非西方年輕聊天機器人用戶團隊分為兩種類型：控制（團隊）和處理（團隊）在參與式 AI 風險評估中。控制團隊從 45 位 AI 實踐者在初步評估中生成的風險列表開始；處理團隊則從我們的框架生成的列表開始。處理團隊總體上識別了更多的風險，並且更多的系統性、人機互動和環境風險。
